definition: Open protocol, hosted by the Linux Foundation, for agents to discover each other through Agent Cards and collaborate over HTTP. Requests and responses use JSON-RPC 2.0.
JSON document in A2A that lists an agent's identity, capabilities, endpoint, skills, and authentication requirements so a client can decide how to call it.
An identity created for an agent so access policy, risk checks, and audit logs can apply to it. Microsoft Entra Agent ID creates these identities from blueprints.

source.title: Overview of agent identities in Microsoft Entra

definition: Signed credential in AP2. A checkout mandate records the cart negotiated with the merchant. A payment mandate authorizes a payment instrument against that checkout.
A market where an agent can hire a specialized agent for a task and pay for the work, or list its own service for other agents to hire.
A wallet an agent can use to discover paid services and pay under a cap the operator set. Tempo Wallet lets an agent preview Machine Payments Protocol terms and pay under a max spend cap.
Open standard for an agent to browse a catalog, run a checkout session, and pass a delegated payment to a business.

source.title: Stripe documentation for the Agentic Commerce Protocol

definition: Open stack, hosted by the Linux Foundation, for cross vendor agent discovery, identity, messaging, and observability.
Open payment extension for A2A and the Universal Commerce Protocol. It records checkout and payment authorization as signed mandates. Public samples exist while FIDO continues the standards work.
A market where independent providers offer compute for workloads. Akash Network documents providers bidding to host those workloads.
A CLP proof bundle that binds signatures, authorization, and payment events into a content-addressed record for an asset or capacity transaction.
A URI that associates a subject with a DID document. The controller can prove control without permission from a centralized registry, identity provider, or certificate authority.
Work product of an open network where independent subnets produce digital commodities and the chain pays contributors.
Draft Ethereum proposal for three registries: an ERC-721 identity that points at an agent registration file, a reputation registry, and a validation registry.
Programmable check that can block, alter, or validate user input, model output, or a tool call. NeMo Guardrails runs these checks as rails around an LLM application.
HTTP status code 402, Payment Required. RFC 9110 reserves the code for future use. x402, L402, and the Machine Payments Protocol use a 402 response as the signal that the request needs payment.
A pause where a person inspects or changes agent state before the run continues. LangGraph provides this inside the graph.
Stateless remote procedure call protocol. A request is a JSON object naming a method, with optional parameters and an id, and the server returns a JSON result or error.
Signed token from Skyfire that binds an agent identity to a payment the buyer has committed. The seller charges the token after delivery.
HTTP 402 flow from Lightning Labs. The server returns a macaroon and a Lightning invoice. The client pays, then presents the preimage so the server can check payment without a lookup.
Open HTTP 402 protocol, co-authored by Stripe and Tempo, so an agent can authorize payment for an API with a card or a stablecoin and receive a receipt.
Open protocol that connects an LLM application to external tools, resources, and prompts. Hosts, clients, and servers exchange JSON-RPC 2.0 messages.
More than one agent collaborating under a runtime. CrewAI pairs event driven Flows for control flow with Crews of role based agents that share a delegated task.
Protocol on A2A 1.0 that lets a personal agent sign its requests and act for a user only inside scopes that user approved with a brand.
A service that verifies a payment and settles it for the seller. In x402 the server asks the facilitator to verify, does the work, then asks the facilitator to settle.

source.title: Coinbase documentation for how x402 works

definition: Draft protocol for a company to publish how a personal agent may sign in and act on a person's account, using OAuth, OpenAPI, and MCP.
Software that returns a decision from policy code, separate from the application that enforces it. Open Policy Agent evaluates structured input against Rego policy.
A budget on model calls. LiteLLM Proxy enforces personal, team, and agent spend budgets when a database is connected.
A function an MCP server exposes for a model to execute. The MCP specification treats a tool as code execution and says hosts must get explicit user consent before invoking one.
Open commerce protocol so agents, businesses, and payment providers can negotiate checkout and identity linking over REST, MCP, or A2A.
Method for an automated client to sign HTTP requests so a site can verify which bot or agent sent them. The signature rules are still an IETF draft.
Open standard for per request HTTP payments. The server quotes a price, the client sends the request again with proof of payment, and a facilitator can verify and settle it.

source.title: Coinbase documentation for how x402 works
